proposals.evidence: Turner specifically assigns Palula y-/yh-, imperative yah and present yhāndu am coming, to yāti. The Palula survey yā- come is therefore this inherited go/come stem; the English elicitation gloss does not justify assigning it to āpayati.

proposals.evidence: Turner groups Khowar diyār, Kalasha/Palula deh, Kashmiri dih, Nepali dinu, Assamese diba and the widespread de-/ḍe- present/imperative series under dadāti, explaining its analogical remodeling with dēti and dēhi. These simple survey di-/de- give forms fit that family. The distinct prā preterite and suffixed past-participial forms are excluded.
